header.noPrev: This is the first record in the list.
header.noNext: This is the last record of the loaded list.

actions.noPermission: You are not allowed to change this record.

shortcuts.cancel: Cancel editing or close the record

sheet.empty: This record has no data to show.

record.notFound: This “{{name}}” record was not found: it may have been withdrawn or be outside your scope.

create.notAllowed: This screen does not allow creating records.

save.noChanges: There were no changes to save.

conflict.title: The record has changed
conflict.description: Someone modified it while you were editing. Compare the values and choose how to go on.
conflict.table: Differences between your changes and the server
conflict.noDifferences: No differences show in the fields being edited; reload to get the current version.
conflict.reloaded: The server version was reloaded and your changes were discarded.
conflict.reapplied: Your changes were put on top of the server version. Review them and save.

discard.title: Unsaved changes
discard.cancel: There are unsaved changes. Do you want to discard them?
discard.leave: There are unsaved changes. If you leave now, they will be lost.

header.title: Record header
header.body: It shows the record, its status and the commands it accepts. The arrows take you to the previous or next record of the list.

tabs.title: Sections
tabs.body: The data is grouped into sections; related tables, such as histories, have their own tab.

save.title: Edit and save
save.body: Press Edit (or the E key) to change the data. Ctrl+Enter saves and Esc cancels; if someone else changed it, you will see the differences before deciding.

child-grid.title: Related table
child-grid.body: The rows related to this record are shown here. They are read-only.

meta.title: Record
meta.body: The record identifier, which you can copy, and its version. When the server sends them, also who created and modified it, and when.

relations.title: Relations
relations.body: The records it is linked to: press one to open its sheet. Where there is a hierarchy, you can also see it in the tree.
